newsitem.title: FINLAND: SIMPLE MAJORITY OK FOR FINNISH PARLIAMENT EMU VOTE.
newsitem.headline: SIMPLE MAJORITY OK FOR FINNISH PARLIAMENT EMU VOTE.

text.p: Parliament's constitutional committee ruled on Wednesday that the assembly can decide by simple majority on Finnish membership of the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU), the committee's secretary said.
The vote is scheduled to take place early next year.
The constitutional committee's decisions cannot be overruled.
It said the government could bring the EMU membership issue to parliament either as a notification or as a regular bill.
The five parties in the left-right-green coalition have 141 MPs in the 200-strong legislature where the speaker does not vote.
Pro-EMU Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's Social Democratic Party is divided on EMU. It has 62 MPs.
Pro-EMU Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's Conservative Party with 39 MPs stands nearly unanimously behind the cabinet's pro-EMU stance.
Most rank and file members of the Leftist Alliance party are against EMU membership, but the party, which has 19 MPs, is seen trying to keep its two cabinet portfolios at almost any cost.
Pro-EMU Europe and foreign trade minister Ole Norrback's Swedish People's Party is officially pro-EMU, but it is not clear whether all its 12 MPs would support membership.
The Green Party, with nine MPs, is openly critical of EMU and has been singled out as a group which might leave government over the single currency.
